Q0603

“On the negative side, avoiding or reversing through a critical conceptual self-awareness…” — Kwasi Wiredu (Q0603)

An English quotation associated with "The Need for Conceptual Decolonization in African Philosophy" (1995), organized here under method.

Quotes / Kwasi Wiredu / Q0603

English

On the negative side, avoiding or reversing through a critical conceptual self-awareness the unexamined assimilation in our thought of the conceptual frameworks embedded in the foreign philosophical traditions that have had an impact on African life and thought. And, on the positive side, exploiting as much as is judicious the resources of our own indigenous conceptual schemes in our philosophical meditations.
Thinker Kwasi Wiredu
School Africana Philosophy
Source "The Need for Conceptual Decolonization in African Philosophy" (1995)
Theme Method

Source context

Archive record: this English passage is associated with "The Need for Conceptual Decolonization in African Philosophy" (1995), within the Africana Philosophy tradition. Use the cited work or edition when a scholarly attribution is needed.

A short reading

Read in the register of method, the sentence asks the reader to test an assumption rather than to collect a slogan. In Kwasi Wiredu's wider work, similar claims are usually offered as prompts for judgment: what would have to be true for the sentence to hold, and what would follow if it did?
